Front: Dataset vs. DataLoader: what does each one own?
Back: Dataset owns single-item access and storage/pointers to the underlying data (__getitem__, __len__). DataLoader owns batch-level concerns: batching, shuffling/sampling, multiprocessing (num_workers), and collating variable-shaped items into a uniform batch.

Front: Why does DataLoader's multiprocessing (num_workers) matter - what's the real mechanism, not 'it uses the GPU'?
Back: It's CPU-side parallelism: multiple worker processes read/transform data concurrently so the next batch can be prefetched while the GPU trains on the current batch. It keeps the GPU fed, it does not offload data loading to the GPU. A naive serial loop (dataset[i] one at a time) starves the GPU with idle wait time between batches.

Front: Bugproof pipelines: what does overfitting a single batch test for, and what's the expected signal?
Back: Isolate one training batch, run the optimization loop against just it repeatedly. Loss should converge to near-zero within a handful of iterations, since correct backprop + correct data should let the model trivially memorize a few examples. If it plateaus/oscillates, that flags a structural bug (broken backprop, bad loss calc, logit/label mismatch, corrupted preprocessing), not a data or capacity issue.
